parts.text:
{
  "first_impression": "Looks like an earnest cozy-indie take on sheepdog trials with clean typography, but the actual 3D art looks a bit sterile and asset-store low-poly. The concept of playing a working border collie dealing with weather, wolves, and stubborn rams is genuinely cool, though whether it holds up depends entirely on sheep AI physics.",
  "scores": {
    "visual_appeal": 6,
    "readability": 8,
    "game_feel": 7,
    "fun_factor": 7,
    "variety": 8,
    "sense_of_progression": 7,
    "want_to_keep_playing": 6,
    "would_wishlist": 7
  },
  "best_things": [
    "The UI presentation, serif typography, and level intro cards nail a warm, classic storybook tone.",
    "Each level genuinely introduces meaningful gameplay wrinkles like stubborn rams, lambs trailing mothers, trials with gate rules, and predators.",
    "The sheep influence ring and control HUD make the herding mechanics look immediately readable and tactical rather than purely chaotic."
  ],
  "worst_problems": [
    {
      "problem": "The water and riverbanks look harsh, flat, and unnaturally cut out from the terrain instead of sitting naturally in a Scottish highland landscape.",
      "where": "evening-5-dawn.jpg",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Rework river mesh edges and add foaming water or soft riverbank blending so it doesn't look like an untextured blue trough carved into the ground."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The night watch predator defense mode turns the game into a dark, flat survival ring that strips away the landscape's charm.",
      "where": "evening-5-night.jpg",
      "severity": "major",
      "suggestion": "Give Pip or the environment better ambient moonlight and distinctive rim lighting so it feels moody instead of muddy and visually empty."
    },
    {
      "problem": "Trees and rocks look like generic low-poly primitives scattered across repeating grass texture with visible tiling seams.",
      "where": "e1-low-view.jpg",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Vary tree foliage models, add denser heather or tufted clumps of grass, and soften the terrain texture repetition."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The shepherd's fold/pen is an empty dirt rectangle with rigid stone walls that looks artificially dropped onto the meadow.",
      "where": "e1-first-home.jpg",
      "severity": "minor",
      "suggestion": "Add clutter, muddy footprints around the gate, wooden hurdle details, and natural slope integration around the pen walls."
    },
    {
      "problem": "The dog's model has sharp angular polygon facets on its head and muzzle that break the otherwise charming border collie silhouette.",
      "where": "evening-5-trial.jpg",
      "severity": "cosmetic",
      "suggestion": "Smooth the normals or increase polycount slightly on Pip's model so the snout and ears look organic rather than blocky cardboard."
    }
  ],
  "boredom_points": [
    "Creeping behind slow-moving sheep across wide empty stretches of grass with nothing happening until the wolf timer ticks down.",
    "The 4+ minute timer on standard maps feels long if you wrap up the main flock early and are stuck searching the corners for one missing ewe."
  ],
  "confusions": [
    "The filename ordering and card numbers jump around (e.g. evening-5-night.jpg says Evening 6: Night Watch in its result screen, while evening-5-trial-card.jpg is labeled Evening 5 The Glenbrae Trial).",
    "In evening-5-trial.jpg, it's not immediately clear from the ground UI how the gate triggers work or which order you must navigate them without checking the minimap text."
  ],
  "wish_list": [
    "Whistle commands or human shepherd audio callouts (Away to Me, Come Bye) instead of just keyboard barking.",
    "Duck or goose herding mini-game mode like real trial novelties.",
    "A cozy free-roam farm mode where Pip can interact with farm animals, rest by the fire, or practice trick runs."
  ],
  "one_line_review": "A surprisingly authentic and structured sheepdog sim hidden behind low-poly visuals - charming if you want real trial tactics, but visually a bit dry."
}
